arabic text: Yaha'n sambhal kar qadam uthana\nYeh baat hargiz na bhul jaana
english translation text: Walk carefully here;\nnever forget this warning.

arabic text: Jahan e sabr o reza yehi hai, Khuda e sabr o reza yaheen hai\nYaha'n pe aate hai chalke Mehdi, Behisht e zahra ye sar zamee'n hai --\nYaha'n hai zahra ka aana jana
english translation text: This is the world of patience and acceptance; the Lord of patience and acceptance is here.\nMahdi comes here on foot, and this land is Zahra's Paradise—\nZahra herself comes and goes here.

arabic text: Duaein denge hussain tumko, yaha'n pe aansu agar bahaye\nJaha'n pe beti ne bewatan ki, sitamgaro se tamache khaye\nYaha'n pe khushiyo ko bhul jaana
english translation text: Hussain will pray for you if you shed tears here,\nwhere the exiled one's daughter was slapped by the oppressors.\nForget every joy when you are here.

arabic text: Yaha'n pe guzri hai wo qayamat, mila na usko sukoon ab tak\nRidaein chinne ke ghum mein abid, lahad mein rota hai khoon ab tak --\nYaha'n pe hargiz na muskurana
english translation text: Such a Judgement Day passed here, and still there is no peace.\nIn grief over the stolen veils, Abid continues to weep blood within his grave—\nnever smile here.

arabic text: Yaha'n pe hurr bhi tha hurmala bhi, kitabe hasti ko padhke dekho\nSada e halmin jo aa rahi hai, tum is taraf ho ya us taraf ho\nTumhe amal se hai ab batana
english translation text: Hurr was here, and Hurmala too; read the book of existence.\nThe call of 'Hal min' still rises: are you upon this side, or upon that?\nYour actions must now provide the answer.

arabic text: Kahi'n pe qasim hue hai tukde, kahi'n pe zee'n se gire the maula\nKahi'n sakina sumo se lipti, kahi'n pe asghar ne teer khaya\nYahi'n ghareebi ka hai thikana
english translation text: In one place Qasim was torn into pieces; elsewhere the Maula fell from his horse.\nAt one place Sakina clung to the horse's hooves; elsewhere Asghar received the arrow.\nThis is the dwelling place of destitution.

arabic text: Sawari aayegi ek waha'n se, najaf ki janib nigaah rakhna\nJab aaye shame ghariba'n jis dum, Ali ko zainab ka pursa dena\nTum aansuo ke diye jalana
english translation text: A rider will come from that direction—keep your gaze towards Najaf.\nWhen the night of the bereaved arrives, offer Zainab's condolences to Ali;\nlight lamps made from your tears.

arabic text: Kisi ke dil mein lagi hai barchi, kisi ke baazu kate yehi par\nHaye ali ki beti ke kitne Yusuf, lahu mein doobe hai is zamee'n par\nLuta hai sadaat ka gharana
english translation text: A spear pierced one heart, and arms were severed here.\nHow many Yusufs belonging to Ali's daughter lie submerged in blood upon this land?\nThe household of the Sayyids was plundered.

arabic text: Rahe kahi'n bhi jaha'n mein jakar, hussain wale ye jaante hai\nHum ehle matam ke dil takallum, yaha'n ki mitti se hi bane hai\nYaha'n hai wapas palatke aana
english translation text: Wherever Hussain's followers may live, they know this:\nO "Taqallum", the hearts of us mourners were formed from this very soil;\nwe must eventually return here.
